articleTitle: The PWM of VSI inverters by output current control in sliding mode
abstract: The PWM of output voltages of a voltage source inverter which feeds a three phase AC motor is described. The AC motor-inverter connection is treated as a uniform system of variable structure. The PWM is given by choice of an appropriate inverter switching state which keeps the sliding mode of the inverter's output current control. The definition of sliding conditions by a modified Lyapunov statement gives a possibility for an optimal choice of the inverter's switching state.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ESC: an expert switching control system
abstract: The paper considers an application of a real-time expert system to controller implementation and offers an alternative to conventional adaptive controllers. The 'expert' is used to switch between different control algorithms so as to achieve high quality control over a range of error signal magnitudes. The aim of the project is to use combinations of simple, well-known controllers with differing response characteristics to achieve better overall control than could be achieved using the control laws separately. The manner and timing of the combination is organised by the 'expert' element. This approach could be regarded as a more sophisticated version of gain scheduling. A further attraction of the approach is that it is well suited to a multiprocessor implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Progress in polynomial optimisation
abstract: The polynomial equation approach to the design of optimal multivariable control systems was pioneered during the 1970's by Kucera. This approach provides a distinctive alternative to the state-space and Wiener-Hopf optimisation procedures. The contribution of this paper is twofold: the author reviews and summarises the major advances made in the polynomial equation approach H/sub 2/ optimisation during the 1980's for multivariable systems; and presents new results concerned with the solution of the H/sub 2/-optimal control problem for the 'standard' control structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fault tolerant controller based on neural nets
abstract: Describes a method of using neural nets of the multi-layer perceptron type in the task of controlling dynamical systems governed by ordinary differential equations which are subjected to a finite set of faults. The set of faults are assumed to be known a priori, although the event itself is considered to occur in a random manner. The proposed controller has the capability to be trained in order to match a reference model, such as a linear second order system. At the occurrence of a fault, the controller is reconfigured by altering the weight values of the synaptic connections according to informations provided by the level of hormones, which is, in the case of animals, a chemical messenger. In this work, the effect of a hormone is simulated by broadcasting a digital signal, indicating the occurrence or not of a fault.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A climbing robot with minimal structure
abstract: The wall-climbing robot 'Zigzag' is one of a succession of mobile robots devised at Portsmouth Polytechnic. Zigzag has but one degree of freedom and strictly has no legs at all. It is controlled at present by direct command from a desk-top computer; when microcontrollers are introduced, each processor will control an entire Zigzag and a supervising microcomputer will direct a team of these robots. The very simplicity of the machine should speed its application and exploitation for tasks including painting, inspection and maintenance of vertical or sloping surfaces.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mixed H/sub 2//H/sub infinity / optimal control of a flexible mechanical servo system
abstract: This paper considers the design of static and fixed order dynamic controllers based on a mixed H/sub 2//H/sub infinity / performance criterion. Necessary conditions are derived for the minimum of a mixed H/sub 2//H/sub infinity / control problem. The design method is applied to a high bandwidth control design problem for a flexible servo system with an uncertain resonance frequency. The H/sub 2//H/sub infinity / controller has been implemented in a digital signal processor. The servo behaviour shows robust performance for the envelope of resonance frequencies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Control of an industrial waste gas scrubber process
abstract: Presents an application of a digital design methodology. The basis of the methodology is the well-known discrete linear quadratic regulator technique. This when applied to the 'non-minimal state-space' (NMSS) representation of Young (1987) leads to a design with natural decoupling. The design algorithm is, however, only one element of an integrated multi-loop design strategy which consists of five distinct stages; sampling time selection, model identification and parameter estimation, controller structure selection, controller design and on-line performance monitoring. The strength of the methodology lies in the tools for automatic sampling time and controller structure selection. These allow the simplest controller configuration to be established that satisfies the chosen performance specifications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Identification of all pole systems with Hermite modulating functions
abstract: When correlation functions are employed with the modulating function method the question arises as to what is the best time relationship between the modulation functions and the correlation functions. This paper explores this matter and finds that there are significant gains in the accuracy of the parameter estimation if the modulating functions are aligned with the peak of the cross-correlation function. Section 2 of the paper briefly reviews the Hermite modulating function method and, gives a matrix technique for estimating errors caused by using a model of order lower than the system order, and analyses the benefits of aligning the modulating functions with the peak of the cross-correlation function formed from the system's input and output signals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fault-tolerant multiple processor system for space instrumentation
abstract: The paper is not based on the design for any single space project but has several ESA, NASA and Soviet projects as the background for the development of a system which will automatically reconfigure itself when a failure occurs. A functional triplicated TMR (triple modular redundancy) configuration is designed which allows the system performance to degrade gracefully after a sequence of individual failures. The distributed system is maintained by use of the 'system information' which is the data which the system holds concerning its own status. The management of multiple redundant copies of this system information allows majority voting, modular fault recovery and system reconfiguration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development of a microprocessor based excitation control system for brushless generators
abstract: Automatic voltage regulators (AVRs) have been used to control the excitation of generators for many years, the early electro-mechanical types being replaced by solid-state regulators utilising power transistors and thyristors controlled by various forms of analogue circuitry. Due to the availability of smaller and more reliable components, together with increased experience, AVRs are now readily available and include many additional features as standard which would previously not have been practical. Economic factors associated with the size of the machine and its application have to be considered but in general the larger the machine, the more sophisticated the specification for the excitation equipment. The current designs of AVR based mainly on analogue circuit techniques have proved very successful and reliable but their relative lack of flexibility has prompted the development of a microprocessor based AVR to overcome this limitation and provide additional facilities. The paper outlines briefly the basic requirements of a microprocessor based AVR targeted for machines ranging from 10 to 200 MW, and describes how the development progressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonlinearity considerations in marine vehicle autopilot design
abstract: Some basic concepts in formulation of various types of ship manoeuvring mathematical models are discussed. Comparison of the two autopilots based on PID and PDF (pseudo-derivative feedback) algorithms showed the superiority of PDF autopilots over PID. Smooth rudder activity and heading responses with smaller overshoots were observed with the PDF autopilot. The results show that with PDF autopilots better performance can be achieved using linear or nonlinear ship models and the PDF autopilot has better transient behaviour and is robust to variation in the parameters and nonlinearities of the ship dynamics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robustness improvement of the F-14 benchmark control problem using H/sup infinity / optimization
abstract: The problem of multivariable control system design has been studied by many researchers. Feedback has been used in control system engineering as a means for satisfying design requirements such as system stabilization, reduction of system response to external disturbances, realization of specified transient response and/or frequency response characteristics, and improvement of a system's robustness against variations in open loop dynamics. The controller for the linearized model of the Grumman aircraft F-14 due to R. Rimer and D.K. Frederick (1987), is redesigned using H/sup infinity / optimisation. The overall system robustness can be improved by changing weights.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of multivariable control to a turbofan engine
abstract: This paper describes the design of a multivariable control for an aeroplane turbofan engine based on working line control. The method starts with the identified engine. Controller performance is illustrated by means of engine test results. The emphasis is on the control structure, which must include the essential features of a complete flight-worthy system, such as all the necessary limiters and a pilot's lever-driven range control, using scheduled gains capable of accommodating parameter variations across the flight envelope. Less importance is attached, at this stage, to the system response attributable to the design of the individual multivariable compensators. In the first instance they were designed as simple P+I controllers. Any changes in the design of the individual compensators can be accommodated within the overall scheme.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An extended qualitative controller
abstract: The application of qualitative reasoning methods in process control is discussed. The work presented is confined to SISO systems with different experimental processes used as application examples. The work shows that pure qualitative knowledge is insufficient to build an efficient controller. Significant improvements can be obtained by combining the qualitative model with process-related quantitative knowledge. The potential advantages of combining qualitative control with state estimation and conventional quantitative control schemes are demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of recursive identification based on delta operators
abstract: Introduces a technique that enables the identification of continuous time transfer function parameters. This has been achieved through the use of the delta operator. It has also been shown how this operator can be used to realise continuous time controllers. The techniques presented have the advantage, that as they operate in the continuous time domain, the coefficients relate to physical quantities. The delta operator has the additional advantage that, provided that the sampling interval is sufficiently short, the coefficients do not change significantly. This suggests that the delta technique could be useful in situations where the sampling rate may change.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of automatic online real-time sampling and analysis and closed loop control of process solutions for electro-plating lines
abstract: Within the steel industry, there is a growing demand to 'close-the loop' in the process control of electroplating lines. Modern plating lines are capable of producing both tinplated and chromium plated steel strip and operate at very high speeds with extremely close tolerances. The paper gives an outline of the work that has already been carried out in this field and describes an exercise that is being progressed jointly by British Steel tinplate and Hilger Analytical Ltd. This current work is being carried out at the former's Trostre Works to establish the feasibility and development of a novel method that uses modern techniques for achieving automatic on-line real-time sampling, analysis and control of the electroplating solutions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer control of pressure die-casting
abstract: The Ford Motor Company (Belfast) Limited manufactures pressurised aluminium die-castings for water pumps and oil pumps for the Ford automobile range. The paper describes a computer monitoring and control system, its development in the Ford plant, and the contribution which this system has made to improved quality in the components being produced. Initially, the system was retro-fitted to five existing die-casting cells but has now been integrated into the controllers for the new cells being delivered. Future plans involve the linking of the entire die-casting area into a computer integrated manufacturing system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An optimal control system for pitch, heave and roll stabilisation of surface vessels
abstract: A six degree of freedom mathematical model is used to compute the motion of a large vessel travelling in head and beam seas. The model is constructed from a set of nonlinear time-varying differential equations and contains fourteen state variables, six control variables and six disturbance variables. Pitch, heave and roll are controlled by two forward and two rear stabilisation fins, each independently controlled. An optimal control law is developed so that the motion is minimised according to some predefined cost function. An optimal solution is sought that provides a global minimum for the important state variables concerned. The extent of the reduced ship motions are analysed and conclusions drawn as to the effectiveness of such a system and whether its implementation can be justified.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of cost effective transputer architectures for the implementation of the computed torque method for robotic manipulators
abstract: The authors address the problem of cost effective architectures for the implementation of the computed torque control method using transputers. They analyse the complexity of the algorithm and as a result compare suitable partitions and their mappings, producing cost effective increases in performance when used to control a model of the Puma 560 robot. Finally, comments are made upon the effect of the inevitable discrepancies between the manipulator and the control model on the choice of architecture.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: H/sub infinity / controller reduction in trajectory sensitivity minimization
abstract: H/sub infinity / optimal control design based on the trajectory sensitivity model is considered. The obtained controller, including the trajectory sensitivity model, is then transformed to a controller which has simple structure. Thereby, controller reduction can be addressed. Since the simplified controller may be unstable itself, a reduction scheme for an unstable transfer function is required. The article considers a left coprime factorization of a part of the generalized plant model and a right coprime factorization (r.c.f.) of the simplified controller so that a Bezout equation holds instead of a doubly coprime factorization. Then, the order of a transfer function which consists of the r.c.f. is reduced. Furthermore, a condition for internal stability in controller reduction is given. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by a numerical example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development of programs for nonlinear control systems in MATLAB
abstract: Three programs useful for teaching various aspects of nonlinear control theory are described. They are all menu driven and run within the MATLAB environment making a major use of the linear control algorithms and graphics facilities therein. Advantage has also been taken of the facility to run FORTRAN programs within MATLAB to make use of existing software, to add other facilities, for example the entry format for transfer functions, and in some instances to speed up calculations. An example is use of the FORTRAN nonlinear algebraic equation solver from the NAG library, as this is found to run much faster than the equivalent MATLAB routine FSOLVE.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust real-time power spectrum estimation
abstract: A recursive robust algorithm for parameter estimation of an AR model, when the scale parameter is also unknown, is considered. First is given the optimal loss function on the class of distributions which is the basis of the criterion generator formulation. Using an approach which is similar to the recursive maximum likelihood methodology, a robust recursive algorithm is derived by criterion minimization. Parameter convergence with probability one is then proved using differential equations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fail-safe control method for programmable electronic systems in railway applications
abstract: The application of microprocessor devices to railway control systems requires very rigorous methods of design, verification and testing. In these systems the safety proof of both hardware and software parts must be established. The fail-safe control considered is realized using special methods recommended by the railway standardization committee (like ORE). The safety measures defined with respect to reliability theory specify the system criteria: mean probability of catastrophic failure (collision, derailment, etc.) or mean time between such failures. The fail-safe computerised railway control realisation is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of multivariable generalised predictive control to a boiler system
abstract: The control of boilers in power stations contributes directly to the efficiency of generation, capability of the plant to respond to changing operating conditions, and plant life. The paper describes the application of generalized predictive control (GPC) to a nonlinear drum boiler-turbine system. The main controlled variables are drum steam pressure and output power, and the inputs are the fuel flow rate and the control valve position.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On-line power systems security assessment
abstract: When a power system state is normal, one must then determine whether it is secure or insecure with respect to the consequences associated with a set of network contingencies. An on-line state estimation and security assessment (SESA) facility has been developed at the National Grid Research and Development Centre, Leatherhead as part of a project for the computer-based operation of a power system. The authors describe enhancements made to ensure the robustness of the security assessment facility and to provide an effective man-machine interface. On-line computation provides an opportunity to use the latest system data and to adopt more refined procedures. The authors will conclude with a prediction of future algorithmic developments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Local actuation of multijointed robotic fingers
abstract: Over recent years a number of advanced multi-fingered grippers have been developed for prosthetic and robotic applications. In all these designs, the crucial question is the location and the type of actuator used to control the individual finger joints. Where the individual finger joints are powered from actuators external to the hand, there is dexterous performance, but considerable problems with power transmission, due to the need to use flexible tendons between the actuators and the individual finger joints. For a multifingered gripper to operate successfully over a wide range of applications, local actuation of the fingers needs to be fully considered, even if there is a reduction in hand dexterity over that of an externally mounted actuator system. The paper reviews a number of possible designs for linkages and actuator that can be incorporated into robotic end effectors and prosthetic hands, including a number built at the University of Southampton.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Approaches to the modelling of biochemical processes
abstract: The paper reports on the development of numerical models for the OTC (oxytetracycline) fermentation process. It also introduces the concept of neural networks and illustrates how these systems can be used to 'learn' the inter-relationships of a fermentation process. The OTC process is outlined and its control problems are highlighted. The development of an AR model for the OTC process is reported. The neural networks and results of a simple network used to model the relationships of some of the variables involved in the OTC process are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fine-grain parallel processing implementations of Kalman filter algorithms
abstract: To implement the Kalman filter, a number of matrix and vector manipulations must be executed within each sample period. Consequently, a drawback of the algorithm is that it is computationally intensive, requiring O(n/sup 3/) operations for each estimate of the n element state vector. Thus, parallel versions of the Kalman filter have been developed in order to reduce execution times and enable the algorithm to be implemented in an increased range of real-time applications. The paper investigates the potential of a 'fine-grain', parallel processing architecture, i.e. the GAPP chip (geometric arithmetic parallel processor), for implementing the Kalman filter algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Loop shaping controller design for a binary distillation column
abstract: Deals with the application of loop shaping controller design methods to a binary distillation problem: The reversed frame normalizing technique and a H/sub $/OI robust stabilization procedure based on a normalized coprime factorization of the plant model are used to design linear multivariable controllers for a distillation column on pilot-plant scale. Basic plant features and the most fundamental aspects of both design techniques are discussed. Experimental evidence is given to illustrate advantages and disadvantages of both methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rapid filters for continuous state-space sensory data acquisition
abstract: Describes a method for high speed input (and state) estimation in continuous state space models, given only discretely sampled output data. The state-space models are considered to describe either single-input/single-output, or more complex multi-input/multi-output (MIMO) sensors operating in continuous time. A full derivation of the algorithms is given, and the performance of such algorithms is discussed in terms of algorithm stability and speed of convergence under initialisation error. It is finally shown how the convergence of the algorithms may be accelerated by considering a slight variation on the conventional state-space equations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple algorithm for robust pole assignment in linear output feedback
abstract: Duan et al. (1990) have proposed a simple, complete and explicit general parametric solution to the eigenstructure assignment of multivariable linear systems via output feedback. Based on this eigenstructure assignment result, and using the condition number type indexes, a very simple algorithm for eigenvalue assignment with minimum sensitivity for linear systems via output feedback is derived. The algorithm derived includes the closed loop eigenvalues in the optimization parameters, and the step of optimization in the algorithm can be carried out independently; hence the optimality of the optimization problem directly implies the optimality of the solution to the problem. A numerical example shows the effect of the proposed algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The multivariable frequency domain toolbox and its relation to other MATLAB toolboxes
abstract: The multivariable frequency domain toolbox supports the analysis and design of multivariable linear feedback systems. The author introduces this toolbox briefly, then go on to point out the versatility of the toolbox, and how it can be used in conjunction with other MATLAB toolboxes. Some industrial applications of the toolbox are described briefly, with indications of how it has been used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A multi-degree of freedom hand powered by two actuators
abstract: Describes a project the aim of which was the development of a dextrous robot hand which would have much of the flexibility of a human hand, yet in volume terms be comparable to the human hand and forearm. In designing a device to these specifications a gripper was produced which was capable of six independent and two dependent degrees of freedom, yet required only two primary motors. Furthermore, this arrangement simultaneously produced an end effector with great stiffness and compliance if required, without the need for a very sophisticated controller.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of feedforward controllers for servo systems in manufacturing applications
abstract: Presents a new approach for the design of tracking controllers using knowledge about the form of the trajectory. If there is a smooth command-path, the tracking-error can be minimized with deadbeat design. The generalised predictive control (GPC) strategy leads to good results, if an optimal control-horizon is chosen. It is pointed out that the GPC strategy uses a position-controller with a regulating function not designed for eliminating disturbances. Experiments showed that model mismatch, limited actuator power and nonlinearities reduce the tracking performance. The closed loop tracking error can be reduced down to 1% of the nominal value without feedforward controller.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Autopilot design for modern missiles
abstract: Concerns the finding of a design method for general cases of missile autopilot design, where yaw and roll control could not be treated as separate SISO systems. This posed the problem of not only finding a linear MIMO design which would be robust but would also be able to compensate for actuator rate and deflection limits safely. Counsell's methodology (1991) for wingless missiles is extended to provide faster and tighter noninteractive response. Furthermore, a criterion for safe control in the presence of gross actuator nonlinearities is described. This criterion is used to determine the maximum yaw rate which the missile can safely achieve. This extended MIMO design allows safe and optimum performance to be achieved with near complete decoupling of roll and yaw manoeuvres.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On finding polynomial controllers with reduced pole sensitivity using state space methods
abstract: The problem of inaccuracies or variations in the parameters of the open-loop model on the poles of the closed-loop system is considered. It is assumed that the system is in input-output form and that the controller design is via pole-placement. The input-output description of the plant does not easily facilitate a direct investigation of the poles of the system. However, the state space description does. This paper presents a different approach to the design of pole-placement controllers for systems in input-output form by transforming to a state space system, performing an output feedback design and transforming the controller back to polynomial form.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A real-time trajectory planner and end-effector collision avoidance control system for a robotic arm
abstract: Describes the design of a real-time trajectory planner, for a robotic manipulator arm, which generates cartesian straight line motions. The design of the trajectory planner facilitates the incorporation of a collision avoidance control system to allow the end-effector to avoid unknown obstacles in the workspace, based on on-line proximity sensor data. The cartesian trajectory, possibly modified by the collision avoidance control system, is then converted into joint coordinates to command the servo-control loops. An experimental version of this trajectory planner has been implemented on a PUMA 562, the details of which are described. The proximity sensing capability is provided by incorporating an array of ultrasonic sensors in the region of the end-effector to detect obstacles being approached by the robot. In order to meet the computational demand of the control systems a multi-processor 68020 VME-based system was used, communicating with the PUMA servo-control boards using Unimation's SLAVE link.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive control by parameter-bounding techniques
abstract: A new approach to adaptive control is described. The aims are robustness and the ability to track both smooth and abrupt time variations in the plant dynamics. The technique is to compute parameter bounds for a plant model, then perform worst-case control synthesis taking account of the uncertainty in the model. Tracking of time variation relies on adaptive adjustment of bounds on the variation of the model parameters, according to the average period of validity of the model. Two control schemes are described for a single-input, single-output plant. The first is a bound-based counterpart of minimum-variance control, employing the L/sub $/OI rather than L/sub 2/ norm to measure performance. The second scheme places the closed-loop poles within specified bounds. In neither scheme need certainty equivalence be adopted, since the model uncertainty is taken explicitly into account in computing the control input.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Feasibility problem of a class of discrete manufacturing process and its solution
abstract: Proposes the feasibility problem of a class of deterministic discrete manufacturing system, explores the operation behavior of such process on the basis of the concepts of partial order set, event graph, sequence matrix, and one-step-backward sequence matrix, develops an algorithm for finding out an optimum prone compatible row sequence matrix, and proves the tenability of the argument, and as such one solution to the problem is obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer aided design package for true digital control (TDC) systems
abstract: The paper outlines briefly the theoretical background to the TDC design procedure, which is based on new methods of input-output state variable feedback control which exploit a non-minimum state space formulation of the control problem using either pole-assignment or linear quadratic optimal control strategies. It then goes on to describe the main features of the computer aided control system design package, which provides the user with assistance at all stages in the design process; from model identification and estimation to final control system design and evaluation, including a rather novel use of Monte Carlo analysis to assess the potential effects of model uncertainty on the closed loop system behaviour.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An evaluation of nonlinear control strategies
abstract: Evaluates the performance capabilities of the controllers designed based upon input-output linearisation theory and the L/A control strategy. After a brief introduction to differential-geometric notation, the fundamental ideas behind the input-output linearisation technique is presented. Next, the L/A control philosophy is discussed in some detail. Finally, the performances of the various control schemes are illustrated by applications to a nonlinear simulation of a continuous bioprocess.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of multifrequency test signals to an industrial water boiler
abstract: To simplify the approach to total plant identification, such that a full understanding of sometimes complicated analyses need not be required, and to present the results of the analyses in a more readable and usable form, the Plant System Identification (PSI) software package was developed. The package follows on from the initial work performed by Mercer and Mailey (1986) using many of the techniques described by Wellstead (1981). This paper describes the salient features of the developed PSI software package which enables rapid modelling of process dynamics, using both frequency and time domain analyses. Emphasis is given to the various multi-frequency type test signal generation and to their practical application to the modelling a 200 KW test boiler.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonlinear adaptive filtering by the Gabor-Kolmogorov method
abstract: Provides an introduction to the Gabor-Kolmogorov model and outlines how the original filter may be easily extended to model multidimensional systems such as those with multiple inputs. Some aspects of the modelling of nonstationary systems are discussed, and a simple procedure to increase the efficiency of the machine is described. Details are also given of past and current applications of the filter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Model reference adaptive control of servodrives
abstract: Interest is focused on model reference adaptive systems (MRAS) which represent an interesting group of adaptive systems for electric drives and their requirements. The basic adaptive model following algorithm is presented. In this case the adaptive mechanism has a PI-character with expressed product nonlinearities. It is necessary to simplify the adaptive mechanism in order to realize the adaptive control of plants with fast dynamics within the available means. For this purpose a modified adaptive algorithm called the unit vector adaptive law, found in the works of Balestrino et al. (1982) is presented. Finally the two presented modified adaptive algorithms are used in the position control of DC servosystems where great changes in the moment of inertia are common. A combined control structure will be used for the needs of positioning. The classical control loop is used for current and position control, and speed control is performed by means of model following control. The advantages of adaptive control over the classical fixed cascade servodrive control are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of decentralized load frequency controller with limited state feedback
abstract: Presents a modified approach for design of decentralized load frequency controller (LFC) for multiarea interconnected power systems. The approach utilizes the eigenvalue dynamics to identify the 'most effective' state-feedback structure of the decentralized controller of the local area to achieve certain stability region. The identification process utilizes the sensitivity of the system eigenvalues for the feedback gains. A new eigenmode analysis are presented that relates the sensitivity of a certain eigenmode with its controllability and observability. The method is illustrated with a simple two-area LFC system, and the time response of the designed controller is compared with the optimal response.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A model library for the control engineering community
abstract: The Model Library described has been developed to provide a set of models more generally acceptable to the broad community of control engineers. Factors which have received particular attention are: industrial acceptability of the models as accurately representing a real industrial plant or process over a well defined range of operating conditions; availability of the model in simulation languages commonly used in both industry and education; comprehensive documentation of each model and the provision of implementation examples; and access to both models and documentation over a well defined range of operating conditions; availability of the model in simulation languages commonly used in both industry and education; comprehensive documentation of each model and the provision of implementation examples; and access to both models and documentation over a well established and widespread computer network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Eigenstructure assignment for aerospace applications: MATLAB implementation
abstract: One of the techniques that have developed from state space formulations of systems is that of eigenstructure assignment. The technique is concerned with the placing of eigenvalues and their associated eigenvectors, by feedback, to meet closed loop design specifications. For a given spectrum of closed loop eigenvalues, the choice of eigenvectors is governed by the number of inputs and outputs. This can be seen by determining the eigenvectors for any eigenvalue. The paper looks at approaches to eigenstructure assignment, their MATLAB realisation, and their application to a simple aerospace example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimal power system stabilizing control by digital redesign technique
abstract: The authors present a practical and efficient approach to design a digital power system stabilizer (PSS) for which the control law of continuous-time systems is reconstructed to make the response of the digital control system as close to that of the continuous-time control system as possible. Alternate digital control laws on the base of redesign techniques (first-order approximation method and second-order approximation method) are applied to determine the control signal for digital PSS. The effectiveness of this proposed method is illustrated using a simulation study of the multi-machine test system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the control of pneumatic positioners and the case of the inverted pendulum
abstract: In a previous paper (see Proc. IEEE Ind. Automation Conf., Toronto, Canada (1990)), the authors applied a model-based control strategy to a system consisting of a rodless cylinder with a 12.5 mm bore, 250 mm stroke and 1.2 kg load. Though previous studies have demonstrated that attractive accuracies and positioning times can be obtained with pneumatic systems under digital control, they were achieved with expensive control valves that provided an air flow proportional to a variable control signal. The present paper describes an investigation of the potential of pneumatic systems controlled by low cost on-off control valves. A pulse-width relay LQR driven controller has been successfully applied to the on-off control of a pneumatic inverted pendulum. The results provide a convincing demonstration of the potential of digitally controlled pneumatic positioners.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of a self-tuning controller to the dynamometer torque loop of an engine test cell
abstract: The engine testing dynamometer, of whatever generic type, is representative of many industrial systems exhibiting fast dynamic behaviour and nonlinear characteristics. In order to provide for effective testing of engines in the light of continuing environmental legislation, conventional manually tuned three term PID controllers are required to be continually adjusted/re-tuned over the performance range of the engine; a time consuming task which neither guarantees optimality or repeatability. This deficiency, coupled with the recent advances in computer technology has prompted the search for alternative control strategies and it is against this background that investigative studies are based. The paper reports on preliminary real-time implementation trials of a pole-placement self-tuning controller applied to the dynamometer torque loop within an engine test cell. The results are encouraging and indicate that potential improvements are possible when employing self-tuning techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Motion management for automotive vehicles
abstract: This paper discusses a study of automotive vehicle control in which the overall aim is the development of a coordinated vehicle control system capable of integrating the actions of the various vehicle subsystems (propulsion, suspension and steering). The study of vehicle control, viewed as a total system composed of interacting subsystems, is introduced as the concept of motion management. The paper presents a brief overview of past and current developments in automotive vehicle control as foundation for discussion of the motion management concept. The paper also considers mathematical modelling techniques and dynamic simulation facilities necessary to support motion management studies in automotive vehicles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive control of systems subject to deterministic time-varying disturbances via an additional measurement
abstract: An additional measurement is introduced into an adaptive control scheme for reducing the undesirable effects caused by the unknown deterministic time-varying disturbances. The additional measurement is utilized in one-step-ahead controller to result in a zero tracking error. It also results in an estimation algorithm, which achieves unbiased parameter estimates without increasing the number of the parameters to be estimated. Global convergence and stability for the closed loop adaptive control systems are established under the ideal condition. Simulation results show that the adaptive control system is stable when the disturbance is actually not a polynomial.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
